newsitem.title: GERMANY: Toepfer sees continued recovery in EU pork output.
newsitem.headline: Toepfer sees continued recovery in EU pork output.

text.p: German grain trader Toepfer said pork production recaptured earlier losses in 1996 as consumers scared away from beef by mad cow disease turned to pigmeat, and output was set to increase in the first quarter of 1997.
Soymeal stands to gain from consumer shifts to pork and poultry because of its higher use in feed rations for those animals compared with cattle and dairy cows, analysts say.
Toepfer said the EU pig count in August was steady from a year ago at 118.2 million animals while numbers in April had been down from a year earlier by one percent at 116 million.
"Expectations are for a continued rise in production well into the first quarter of 1997," it said.

EU beef consumption plummeted in March after the British government said mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), may be linked to a fatal human brain disease. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
